notes.text: Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 12 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Taylor Hall is out, reported after he played in their last game.

Alexander Nikishin is day to day (not injury related) and has missed the last 10 games. Juuso Välimäki has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere. That pair has had 70% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 93:50 together.
Jared McCann is out 10 weeks (lower body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Matthew Wood joined from NSH on Nov 2 and has played beside Chandler Stephenson and Frédérick Gaudreau.
Vince Dunn has started killing penalties: on the ice for 42% of the team’s shorthanded time in 15 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the NHL with 28 points, the Kraken tied for third in the Pacific with 19 points.

SEA.head: The Kraken have their work cut out
SEA.body: Even though Seattle has home-ice advantage and gets Fleury back, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Seattle will be without McCann. The Kraken can still win it if they keep dangerous shots away, but a lot has to go their way.

story.head: The Hurricanes are going to let it fly
paras: The Hurricanes (13-3-2) beat the Islanders 5-3 on Nov 5, and the Kraken (9-5-1) beat Calgary 2-1 in overtime on Nov 4. Going in, the Hurricanes are first in the NHL and the Kraken third in the Pacific (tied for 14th in the NHL).
The Hurricanes’ record (.778) is about what their chances are worth. The Kraken’s record (.633) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.455), largely thanks to their finishing.

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). The Kraken, by contrast, rarely threaten on the penalty kill (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.83 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.33, the third fewest. On the other side, the Kraken keep dangerous shots away better than anyone (1st). They also give up a lot of shots (32nd), so the Hurricanes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against them. The Canes’ forecheck could keep the Kraken pinned in their own end.

Sebastian Aho (9 G / 14 A / 23 P in 18 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for ninth in the NHL, and Logan Stankoven (11 G / 6 A / 17 P in 18 GP) has a team-high eleven goals, tied for sixth in the NHL. For the Kraken, Berkly Catton (5 G / 7 A / 12 P in 15 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Frédérick Gaudreau (7 G / 3 A / 10 P in 15 GP) has a team-high seven goals.

Pyotr Kochetkov (10-1-0 / .921 SV% in 11 GS) has been terrific for Carolina and will likely start. Seattle has two options in net: Philipp Grubauer (5-2-1 / .886 SV% in 8 GS) and Joey Daccord (4-3-0 / .889 SV% in 7 GS). Grubauer has started six of their last ten games, but Daccord got the last one on Nov 4. It’s anyone’s guess who gets the net.

At home, Lane Lambert likes to send Nyman, Meyers and Winterton out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Deslauriers. One more thing: the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Kraken do.

items.text: The Hurricanes are newly without Taylor Hall, and have been without Jordan Staal and Alexander Nikishin for several games.
The Kraken have been without Jared McCann since Oct 22.
Jesperi Kotkaniemi has five goals on chances worth about 1.3 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.
Jackson Blake has a point in eight straight games.
